title: bug: the claude-plugin daemon client ignores MOE_DAEMON_HOST, so in WSL agent mode its PostToolUse hook and callTool dial 127.0.0.1, which the Windows daemon never answers, and every AGENT_TOOL_EVENT is lost
description:
Filed by defect hunt 11-03 #3 (task-859eff80). This is the hunt #2 "host vs bindHost" item, now with evidence that it matters.

PROBLEM
- packages/moe-claude-plugin/src/daemonClient.ts:149 sets the connect host to daemon.json `host`, else '127.0.0.1'. The daemon never writes `host`. It writes `bindHost`, which is "wsl" in WSL agent mode. So the plugin always dials loopback. sendOnce (:237) uses that host for both callTool (/mcp) and postEvent (/ws, which the PostToolUse hook uses).
- Nothing in packages/moe-claude-plugin/src reads MOE_DAEMON_HOST (0 grep hits). moe-proxy does: packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts:69-73 getDaemonHost() returns MOE_DAEMON_HOST, else '127.0.0.1'. docs/CONFIGURATION.md:44 and :61 document MOE_DAEMON_HOST as the connect-host override "for agents + spawned MCP servers (WSL mode)". docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:187 says it overrides the client's destination. The wrapper exports it for WSL seats; this seat has MOE_DAEMON_HOST=172.26.208.1.
- Consequence: under WSL NAT networking, loopback inside WSL is not the Windows host.
  - The hook's AGENT_TOOL_EVENT never reaches /ws, so server/WebSocketServer.ts:1016-1058 never folds toolCalls into task metrics (util/metrics.ts:22), and the IDE never sees the seat's tool activity.
  - The failure is swallowed, because the hook fails open.
  - README.md:75 then tells the user that CONNECT_FAILED means the daemon crashed.
- Scope note: no seat in this fleet has the plugin installed today (0 AGENT_TOOL_EVENT in .moe/activity.log 09:13Z-16:12Z). The bug hits WSL-mode users who install the plugin.

EVIDENCE
1. Live, from a WSL seat at 2026-11-03 16:16Z, with daemon.json bindHost "wsl" and port 9876:
   - `curl -s -m 3 http://127.0.0.1:9876/health` exits 7 (connection refused);
   - `curl -s -m 3 http://172.26.208.1:9876/health` returns HTTP 200.
2. Repro on HEAD ef5c7101 in /tmp/hunt-859e-snap (git archive with Linux node_modules). Persisted copies: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-859e/zzHunt859ePluginHost.test.ts and plugin-host.output.txt. Command: `cd packages/moe-claude-plugin && npx vitest run tests/zzHunt859ePluginHost.test.ts`. Result: 2 failed.
   - findDaemonInfo, with MOE_DAEMON_HOST=172.26.208.1 and daemon.json {bindHost:"wsl"}: `expected '127.0.0.1' to be '172.26.208.1'`.
   - callTool, against a ws server listening only on 127.0.0.2 with MOE_DAEMON_HOST=127.0.0.2: `DaemonError: Cannot reach daemon at 127.0.0.1:38559: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:38559` (code CONNECT_FAILED).
3. Dry run of the fix direction (line 149 reads MOE_DAEMON_HOST first):
   - With MOE_DAEMON_HOST unset, the repro plus tests/daemonClient.test.ts and tests/postToolUse.test.ts pass 20/20.
   - With the seat's inherited MOE_DAEMON_HOST=172.26.208.1, three EXISTING tests then fail because they assume loopback: 'accepts a 65536-byte daemon.json', 'forwards a tools/call request and returns the result', and 'forwards moe.* tool events with the expected envelope'. So the fix must make those suites hermetic.

FIX DIRECTION
- Resolve the connect host the way the proxy does: a non-blank MOE_DAEMON_HOST first, then a legacy daemon.json `host` string, then '127.0.0.1'.
- Never use `bindHost` as a connect address: "wsl" is a bind mode.
- In the tests, clear MOE_DAEMON_HOST for the loopback suites (for example vi.stubEnv in beforeEach), so they pass on a WSL seat that exports it.
- Add one README troubleshooting line: on WSL, CONNECT_FAILED means MOE_DAEMON_HOST is unset or wrong.

FILES: packages/moe-claude-plugin/src/daemonClient.ts, tests/daemonClient.test.ts, tests/postToolUse.test.ts (the hermetic env only) and README.md. None is held by an open row (lanes.js at 16:21Z). CI runs the plugin tests on ubuntu-latest only (.github/workflows/ci.yml:81-100), so a 127.0.0.2 listener works there. Guard it with a skip where that address cannot be bound (macOS).
definitionOfDone: With a non-blank MOE_DAEMON_HOST, findDaemonInfo returns it as `host`, ahead of daemon.json's `host`. A blank or unset value falls back to daemon.json `host`, then '127.0.0.1'. `bindHost` is never used as a connect host.

A new test starts a WebSocket server on a non-default loopback address (127.0.0.2, skipped where that address cannot be bound) and writes daemon.json with bindHost "wsl" and no `host`. It sets MOE_DAEMON_HOST to that address and asserts that callTool resolves and postEvent's frame reaches the server. Restoring today's daemonClient.ts:149 fails it.
The existing daemonClient and postToolUse tests pass with unchanged assertions, both with MOE_DAEMON_HOST unset and with it set to 172.26.208.1, because their env setup is now hermetic.

Verification, in a snapshot outside the shared checkout: `cd packages/moe-claude-plugin && MOE_DAEMON_HOST=172.26.208.1 npx vitest run && env -u MOE_DAEMON_HOST npx vitest run && npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.

implementationPlan.description:

(1) `grep -n bindHost packages/moe-claude-plugin/src/daemonClient.ts` hits only comments.
(2) The env is read on every call, so a stub set after import still takes effect.
(3) A blank or whitespace MOE_DAEMON_HOST, and a blank legacy `host`, both fall through to the next source.
(4) DoD 3: in the test files, the only removed line is daemonClient.test.ts's import line (`git diff -U0 <base> -- packages/moe-claude-plugin/tests | grep '^-[^-]'`), and no existing expect changed.

(8) No .only or stray .skip is left, there is no console noise, and tracked files were written only with Edit/Write.
Check the edge cases too:
- two hook processes running concurrently share no state;
- an IPv6 literal in MOE_DAEMON_HOST is out of scope (the proxy does not bracket one either).

executionContract.intendedBehavior: The Claude Code plugin's daemon client dials a non-blank (trimmed) MOE_DAEMON_HOST first, then a non-blank legacy daemon.json `host`, then 127.0.0.1. This applies to callTool (/mcp) and to postEvent (/ws, which carries the PostToolUse hook's AGENT_TOOL_EVENT). daemon.json's `bindHost` is never dialed. The plugin's loopback test suites no longer depend on the MOE_DAEMON_HOST that a WSL seat inherits.
acceptanceCriteria: findDaemonInfo(...).host equals MOE_DAEMON_HOST.trim() whenever that is non-empty, whatever daemon.json's host or bindHost says.
An unset or blank MOE_DAEMON_HOST falls back to a non-blank daemon.json `host`, else '127.0.0.1'. bindHost ('wsl' or an IP-looking value) is never returned.

Take a daemon listening only on 127.0.0.2, daemon.json {bindHost:'wsl'} with no host, and MOE_DAEMON_HOST=127.0.0.2. callTool resolves and postEvent's frame arrives on /ws. With today's daemonClient.ts:149 the same case fails with CONNECT_FAILED at 127.0.0.1.
The pre-existing daemonClient and postToolUse tests pass with unchanged assertions, both with MOE_DAEMON_HOST unset and with it set to 172.26.208.1.
The README Troubleshooting section says that on WSL, CONNECT_FAILED means MOE_DAEMON_HOST is unset or wrong.
invariants: bindHost is never read as a connect address.
MOE_DAEMON_HOST is read on every findDaemonInfo call, never cached at module load.
These stay unchanged: the wire format (handshake, frames, the /mcp and /ws paths), the timeouts, the DaemonError codes, and the hook's fail-open error handling.
No existing test assertion is changed or removed.
compatibility: With MOE_DAEMON_HOST unset, every existing daemon.json resolves exactly as before: the legacy `host` is honored, otherwise 127.0.0.1.
DaemonInfo keeps its field names and its optional `host`. Callers of findDaemonInfo, callTool and postEvent need no change.

packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:876 writes bindHost only when non-loopback, and the daemon never writes host.
scripts/moe-agent.sh:1902 exports MOE_DAEMON_HOST after WSL host discovery.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Rejected four alternatives:
(1) Dial bindHost when it looks like an IP. bindHost is a bind mode ('wsl', '0.0.0.0'), and the daemon and proxy never dial it either.
(2) A vitest setupFiles entry that clears the env. It touches vitest.config.ts and adds a new file, while file-scope hooks keep each suite self-contained.
(3) A platform === 'darwin' skip. A bind probe that skips only on EADDRNOTAVAIL never silently skips on Linux or Windows.
(4) Exporting resolveConnectHost for direct unit tests. The DoD asserts through findDaemonInfo, so the helper stays private.
I dry-ran the exact plan on d5f36e82 in a scratch copy:
- red: 3 failed / 20 passed with today's src;
- green: 23/23 with MOE_DAEMON_HOST=172.26.208.1 and with it unset, and tsc clean;
- mutants: the original postToolUse.test.ts with the fixed src fails 'forwards moe.* tool events' after a 3009 ms timeout to the gateway, so the hermetic hooks are load-bearing; an untrimmed-env mutant fails the blank case.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The daemon writes bindHost only when it binds non-loopback, and it never writes host (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:876).
- moe-proxy's getDaemonHost is `MOE_DAEMON_HOST || '127.0.0.1'` (packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts:72-74).
- scripts/moe-agent.sh:1902 exports MOE_DAEMON_HOST after WSL host discovery, so the claude CLI and its PostToolUse hook child inherit it.
- WebSocket upgrades are guarded by the Origin rule, not by Host (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:674-678). A gateway IP in the client's Host header is therefore fine.
- vitest 5.0.5: stubEnv(name, undefined) deletes the var; unstubAllEnvs restores it; vi.waitFor exists; ESM test files allow top-level await.
- tsconfig includes src only, so `tsc --noEmit` checks src.
- CI runs the plugin tests on ubuntu-latest only (ci.yml, test-typescript job).
- The plugin lock already lists @rolldown/binding-linux-x64-gnu 1.2.15, and /tmp/hunt-859e-snap holds a Linux node_modules for that byte-identical lock.
planningNotes.risks:
- Put the env hooks at file scope, not inside one describe. Otherwise the size-cap and callTool describes stay exposed.
- postEvent resolves about 25 ms after it writes, so wait for the frame with vi.waitFor rather than a fixed sleep.
- Do not run npm in the shared checkout or in the worktree. Use the /tmp snapshot in step 3.
- QA re-run: `git archive <completion sha> packages/moe-claude-plugin | tar -x -C $S/...`, with no working-tree overlay, then the same checkRef. For red, swap in `git show <sha>^:packages/moe-claude-plugin/src/daemonClient.ts`: the 3 new cases must fail.
- IPv6 literals are out of scope.
